fixes.explanation: Right, baker. Jesus says, "What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops." So what's whispered in their ears is meant to be spoken out loud. I think that's the biggest volume change I've ever heard of, from a whisper straight to a rooftop.

The verses just before tell the disciples to speak in the daylight and proclaim from the housetops. But Jesus says, "Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul." It's a heavy line, so I'll leave it there. The soul is the answer.

Jesus says, "Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father." Those are two sparrows sold for a penny, baker. And still the Father's will is in the picture for every one. I think that's the whole point of the comparison.
Jesus says, "So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows." He says it right after the sparrows and the numbered hairs. Baker, not just more than one sparrow, but MORE than many.

Jesus sets the bar much higher. He says, "you are worth more than many sparrows." Two sparrows is just the penny price He mentions two verses earlier. Many sparrows is a lot more than two, and you're worth more than that.
It's the other direction, baker. Jesus says, "you are worth more than many sparrows." Not less than one, but more than many. He begins that verse with "So do not be afraid…" and I think this is why.

Jesus says, "Do not assume that I have come to bring peace to the earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword." The next verses show what He means, baker, a man against his father, a daughter against her mother. I'd say that's one to read slowly.

Earlier Jesus actually tells the disciples to take no staff for the journey (Matthew 10:10). Here He says, "…anyone who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me." The thing to take up is a cross, not a staff, baker.
Jesus doesn't say waste. He says, "…whoever loses his life for My sake will find it." Losing it for His sake ends in finding, baker, not waste.

Jesus says, "Whoever receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward…" Receiving a prophet because he is a prophet comes with a prophet's reward. Baker, I think that's a generous deal. He says the same about receiving a righteous man because he is a righteous man.

Friends are great, baker, but they're not what Jesus names. He says, "…truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward." That's for giving even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is His disciple. The word is reward.

Home is a good thing to keep, baker. But Jesus says, "…truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward." He says it about anyone who gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is His disciple. The word is reward.

A mountain, baker? I read that verse looking for one, and nope. Matthew 11:1 says, "After Jesus had finished instructing His twelve disciples, He went on from there to teach and preach in their cities." Teaching and preaching in their cities is what He does next.
